About Lares
Version %1$s Version %1$s\n\nLares blocks the apps and websites you choose. Adding restrictions is always possible – loosening them needs a code that only your guardian knows.\n\nFree software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. Privacy policy Everything stays on this phone Lares works entirely on this phone.\n\n• No account, no analytics, no advertising, no tracking.\n• No data is sold or shared with third parties.\n• Your rules, usage times and settings are stored only on this phone. They are excluded from Android backups and device transfers.\\\n• If you turn on the Accessibility service or usage access, Lares uses it only to detect which app (or website) is open. This is processed on the phone in the moment and neither stored nor sent.\n• Lares connects to the internet only to send guardian notifications – and only to the services set up in the settings (Telegram, ntfy, email, Matrix or a webhook). These messages contain only the notification text (e.g. “protection was disabled”) and the phone model; tokens are stored encrypted on the phone.\n• The guardian code is stored only as a protected hash (password) or encrypted with a key that never leaves this phone (authenticator app).\n• Lares blocks password managers, so the guardian code is never saved on the phone. License GNU GPL, version 3 or later Lares is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.\n\nLares is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. Not chosen yet Choosing the mode for the first time is free; switching it later needs the guardian code. Website blocking Blocks websites in supported browsers; other browsers are blocked completely. Prevent uninstalling Android refuses to uninstall Lares (device administrator). Guard system settings Blocks the system pages for force-stopping or uninstalling Lares and for its permissions. Needs the Accessibility service. Restart after reboot Starts protection again after a restart or app update and records gaps. Notify guardian Informs the guardian about tampering, e.g. a disabled protection or repeated wrong codes.

Blocking isn’t fully set up yet Recommended Battery optimization is on Android may pause Lares in the background, so blocking stops working – especially on Xiaomi, Huawei, Samsung, OnePlus and similar phones. Set Lares to “Not optimized” / “Unrestricted”. Some phones also have an extra “Autostart” or “Sleeping apps” setting. Tips for your phone Open system settings No blocking mode chosen Choose how Lares detects open apps. Recommended: the Accessibility service. Choose mode Accessibility service is off Needed for the (recommended) Accessibility blocking mode, for website blocking and for guarding the system settings. Turn on “Lares” under installed or downloaded apps. Usage access missing Needed in the “Usage access” mode to detect which app is open. Allow it for Lares. “Display over other apps” missing Needed in the “Usage access” mode to show the block screen. Allow it for Lares. Uninstall protection isn’t active “Prevent uninstalling” is on, but Lares isn’t a device administrator yet. Activate While active, Android refuses to uninstall Lares. Lares uses no other administrator rights. Accessibility service Lares uses Android’s Accessibility service to find out which app is open – and, if website blocking is on, which website is shown in the browser – so it can block what you chose.\n\nThis information is used only on this phone, in the moment. It is not stored and never sent anywhere.\n\nOn the next screen, open “Lares” (under installed or downloaded apps) and turn it on. Agree and continue
Lares detects which app or website is open to block the ones you chose. Nothing is stored or sent.
